field_matches.expected: GBA mutations have been associated with Parkinson's disease in numerous studies; established in patients with two GBA alleles (Gaucher disease) and in single-mutation carriers (heterozygotes)
Missense (e.g. N370S, L444P, R496H); 84GG and other GBA mutations/variants
Mutations lead to reduction in glucocerebrosidase enzymatic activity; N370S retains 30% of enzymatic activity

Up to 6% of Ashkenazi Jews are carriers of GBA mutations; N370S is the most common Gaucher mutation in Ashkenazi Jews; LRRK2 G2019S is the most common autosomal dominant mutation in the Ashkenazi Jewish population
Parkinson's disease (UK Parkinson's Disease Brain Bank criteria); assessed with UPDRS and Montreal Cognitive Assessment
Glucocerebrosidase enzymatic activity in dried blood spots (mmol/l/h)
Patients with Parkinson's disease were more likely to be male than controls (by design, spouse controls)
Mixed cohort with assessment of Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry; patients and controls similar in Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry
LRRK2 G2019S described as autosomal dominant mutation

Cases defined by UK Parkinson's Disease Brain Bank criteria (family history not excluded); sensitivity analysis excluded onset <=40 years to remove potential parkin (PARK2)/PINK1 cases that were not tested
All participants genotyped for LRRK2 G2019S mutation
Genotyping for 10 GBA mutations/variants and LRRK2 G2019S, followed by full sequencing of the GBA gene in all patients and controls

DNA extracted by salting-out; PCR with AmpliTaq Gold; Sanger sequencing on 3730XL DNA Analyzer; chromatograms analysed with Genalys 3.3b; sequencing success rate 96%; all mutations detected by screening replicated by sequencing
For Parkinson's disease cases with compound heterozygote GBA mutations/variants, family members were analysed to confirm whether mutations were in cis (same allele) or trans (opposite allele)
Compound heterozygote phase confirmed via family member analysis
Cis (same allele) versus trans (opposite allele) determined by family analysis for compound heterozygotes
Seven GBA homozygotes and compound heterozygotes among Parkinson's disease patients
Among controls, 17 GBA heterozygotes (6.7% of 252); 35.2% (6 of 17) of control GBA carriers reported at least one Ashkenazi Jewish grandparent; up to 6% of Ashkenazi Jews are GBA carriers
Glucocerebrosidase enzymatic activity assay (lysosomal enzyme activity)

Dried blood spots; mass spectrometry-based (tandem MS/MS) multiplex assay measuring glucocerebrosidase and four additional lysosomal enzymes; API 4000 triple quadrupole mass spectrometer with Multiple Reaction Monitoring

Lower glucocerebrosidase enzymatic activity strongly associated with GBA mutations and modestly with idiopathic Parkinson's disease; GBA homozygotes/compound heterozygotes < GBA heterozygotes < non-carriers; LRRK2 G2019S carriers had higher activity than non-carriers

Homozygotes/compound heterozygotes 0.85 mmol/l/h vs heterozygotes 7.88 mmol/l/h (P<0.001); heterozygotes 7.88 vs non-carriers 11.93 mmol/l/h (P<0.001); all PD 11.14 vs controls 11.85 mmol/l/h (P=0.011); idiopathic PD 11.53 vs controls 12.11 mmol/l/h (P=0.036); LRRK2 G2019S carriers 13.69 vs non-carriers 11.93 mmol/l/h (P=0.002); per-mutation reductions N370S P<0.001, L444P P<0.001, 84GG P=0.003, R496H P=0.018, E326K P=0.009, T369M P<0.001
Disease positive samples included in each plate for quality control
Blank filter paper background activity subtracted from dried blood spot activity

Two quality control samples with previously established activity levels for each enzyme included on each plate; each batch included at least three replicates of two quality control samples with established activity ranges; sample activity normalized to mean of QC samples from same run
Student t-test, ANOVA, chi-square, Fisher's exact test, Pearson correlation, logistic regression; P values reported; activity normalized to batch QC controls
Glucocerebrosidase enzymatic activity measured directly in patient dried blood spots (whole blood)
Patient-derived material (dried blood spots / whole blood)
Loss of glucocerebrosidase function proposed to contribute to pathogenesis of Parkinson's disease; high activity in LRRK2 G2019S carriers may reflect a distinct pathogenic mechanism
Reduced enzymatic activity (e.g. N370S retains 30% activity)
Reduced glucocerebrosidase enzymatic activity consistent with proposed loss-of-function mechanism
Validated dried blood spot methodology (Zhang et al., 2008) clinically approved to screen for Gaucher disease; Genzyme scientists blinded to Parkinson's disease and genetic status
Case-control comparison of Parkinson's disease patients and non-blood related controls (mostly spouses) from Columbia University Medical Center
Parkinson's disease per United Kingdom Parkinson's Disease Brain Bank criteria (cases with family history not excluded)
Non-blood related controls, mostly spouses; patients and controls similar in age, education and Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry; patients more likely male by design
GBA mutations/variants 17.0% (88: seven homozygotes/compound heterozygotes and 81 heterozygotes); LRRK2 G2019S 7.5% (39)
GBA mutations/variants P<0.001; LRRK2 G2019S P<0.001; glucocerebrosidase activity PD vs controls P=0.011 (idiopathic PD P=0.036; adjusted P=0.012)
Student t-test, chi-square test, Fisher's exact test, ANOVA, Pearson correlation, logistic regression (SPSS Statistics v19.0)
Evaluation of Parkinson's cases and controls was identical; all participants fully sequenced for GBA and genotyped for LRRK2 G2019S; Genzyme scientists blinded to disease and genetic status
Spouse controls leading to sex imbalance (patients more likely male); analyses adjusted for age and gender

Most GBA homozygotes and compound heterozygotes (Gaucher disease patients) will never develop Parkinson's disease despite diminished glucocerebrosidase enzymatic activity, suggesting an additional mechanism

GBA encodes the lysosomal enzyme glucocerebrosidase, a glucosylceramide hydrolase that plays an important role in sphingolipid degradation, especially in the macrophage/monocyte cell lineage; diminished activity in Gaucher disease causes glucocerebroside accumulation in spleen, liver and bone marrow
Lysosomal enzyme; activity prominent in macrophage/monocyte cell lineage

Reduced glucocerebrosidase enzymatic activity in GBA mutation carriers' blood; prior report of increased cytosolic reactive oxygen species in fibroblasts from GBA heterozygotes with and without Parkinson's disease (McNeill et al., 2014)
All GBA mutations detected by screening were replicated by full sequencing
N370S linked to Type 1 (non-neuronopathic) Gaucher disease; GBA mutations previously associated with Gaucher disease
